issues.description: Endpoint path names for the Person API are inconsistent between the problem statement, the client implementation and the server implementation in the solution. The problem statement explicitly lists endpoints under /persons (POST /persons, GET /persons, PUT /persons/{personId}, DELETE /persons/{personId}). The solution's client-side PersonController issues requests to URIs under "persons" (e.g. .uri("persons")), but the solution's server-side PersonResource registers its endpoints under "people" (e.g. @GetMapping("people")). This mismatch prevents the client and server from communicating and contradicts the specified API in the problem statement, creating confusion for students implementing or testing the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the URI paths consistent with the problem statement and between client and server. Preferably change the server-side mappings in src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java from "people" to "persons" (e.g. @GetMapping("persons"), @PostMapping("persons"), @PutMapping("persons/{personId}"), @DeleteMapping("persons/{personId}")), or alternatively update the client to use "people" — but ensure the chosen path matches the problem statement and is used consistently in both client and server. Update any documentation in problem_statement.md if a different path is intentionally preferred.

issues.description: The Problem Statement specifies REST endpoints under /persons (POST /persons, GET /persons, PUT /persons/{personId}, DELETE /persons/{personId}), but the solution's server-side PersonResource exposes endpoints under /people while the solution's client-side PersonController issues requests to /persons. This creates a conflicting naming for the same conceptual entity (persons) across artifacts and between client and server in the solution, and does not match the problem specification — causing students to be unable to map requirements to the implemented endpoints.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the identifier to match the Problem Statement. Change the server-side mappings in src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java from "people" to "persons" for all endpoints (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) so they match /persons and the client requests. Alternatively, if you prefer "people", update the Problem Statement and all client code to use "people" consistently — but keep client and server names identical.
